claim.qualifier: Tesla advertises Model Y Long Range AWD 0–60 with 1-foot rollout
claim.verbatim_quote: Tesla, like many manufacturers, uses a 1-foot rollout method in official performance testing. This means timing starts once the car moves its first foot — slightly improving recorded times.

sources.name: Autoguide — Tesla Model Y 0–60 Time documentation of rollout convention

reality.qualifier: Car and Driver instrumented 0–60 for 2026 (refreshed) Model Y Long Range AWD, with 1-foot rollout omitted (0.3 sec). MotorTrend measured 3.8 sec.
reality.verbatim_quote: Our 60-mph test came back at 3.9 seconds … Results above omit 1-ft rollout of 0.3 sec.

sources.name: Car and Driver — 2026 Tesla Model Y Long Range AWD instrumented test
MotorTrend — 2026 Tesla Model Y Long Range AWD First Test Review

narrative_one_liner: Tesla's 0–60 figures use 1-ft rollout; instrumented tests without rollout are 0.2 sec slower (~5%).
narrative: Tesla's published 0–60 time uses 1-foot rollout (timing starts after the vehicle has moved one foot, ~0.3 sec). Independent instrumented testing without rollout measures 3.9 sec (Car and Driver) and 3.8 sec (MotorTrend) for the refreshed 2026 model. The gap is small but systematic and complicates apples-to-apples comparison with manufacturers that don't use rollout.
methodology_notes: Both Car and Driver and MotorTrend use VBOX-style instrumented timing on private test surfaces. Both publications explicitly disclose rollout treatment in their methodology sections.
caveats: The 'claim' figure (4.1 s) is a representative number for the LR AWD trim; Tesla's published number on the configurator page can vary by software version and wheel choice.
Industry-standard: most manufacturers use 1-foot rollout. The deception is in the lack of disclosure, not in the practice itself.
alternative_explanations: Battery state-of-charge and temperature affect 0-60; both publications conducted tests in conditions documented in their reports.
Refreshed model year (2026) measured here may differ from earlier generations.
